Subject: PoC / Trial plan and deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme

Hi John,

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciated the detailed run-through of Acme's high-throughput inference use case. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- High sustained qps for multi-tenant inference (peak 1.2k qps expected), low tail latency requirement (~200ms P95).
- Data residency and isolation are important for the initial rollout (legal + internal policy).
- Integration with internal SSO and audit logging is required for compliance.

Initial deployment-mode recommendation (based on call):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) looks like the best fit for predictable throughput + isolation.
- Hosted API could be used as a fast short-term path for early exploration, but may not satisfy isolation/compliance for production.
- Private VPC/on-prem is an option if procurement/legal insist on customer-managed network boundary — we should confirm network constraints.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (attached: redwood-poc-plan-acme.xlsx):
- Duration: 3 weeks (2-week technical validation + 1-week performance tuning).
- Success criteria:
  1) Achieve sustained 1k qps with <=250ms P95 on the agreed model variant.
  2) End-to-end request latency from Acme front-end to response under 300ms.
  3) Verify audit logs, SSO integration, and data retention controls.
- Stakeholders to involve: Engineering (API owners), Security/Compliance, Procurement.
- Proposed kickoff: Mon, 2 Mar (open to shifting).

Can you confirm: (a) the primary stakeholders we should invite (names and emails), (b) whether procurement needs a formal quote/PO before we start the PoC, and (c) whether you'd prefer we start with Hosted API to shorten time-to-first-test or go straight to Dedicated?

I've cc'd Lauren (CSM) to coordinate scheduling and Logan (SE) will follow up with a short technical checklist once we align on approach.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi John / Ben —

Thanks — looping in a few technical details to help you evaluate options and to scope the PoC: 

Quick summary of differences relevant to your success criteria:
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, no infra changes required. We can enable structured audit logs (delivered to a secure bucket) and API keys tied to your account. Limitations: can't provide network-level isolation or customer-managed KMS in Hosted.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools. Provides tenant isolation at the compute layer, predictable throughput, and stronger SLA. Can integrate with your SSO and centralized logging via our syslog/Kinesis connectors.
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer-managed network boundary and KMS/HSM options. Requires network peering or a VPN (we support AWS VPC peering, PrivateLink in supported regions, or site-to-site VPN for on-prem).

For the PoC I recommend a two-track approach:
1) Functional validation on Hosted API (1 week): confirm model outputs, auth flow, logging format.
2) Performance validation on Dedicated (2 weeks): run load tests to validate sustained qps and latency.

Required inputs for Dedicated sizing for your 1.2k qps target:
- Model choice and typical token length distribution (avg/95th).
- Expected concurrency per client.
- Acceptable P95 latency target (you mentioned ~200ms).

I've attached a sample PoC config (poc-configuration.yaml) with suggested instance types and batch sizing for the Dedicated run. Also putting a link to a short runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-redwood-poc-acme

Network requirements (high level):
- If you choose Private VPC: allow outbound to 34.200.0.0/12 (example), TCP 443, and set up a route for peering. We'll provide exact IP ranges for the selected region prior to kickoff.

Ben — happy to join the kickoff to walk through the runbook and baseline scripts.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
